tagline: County lines and a river divide shape a road through Southside Virginia
intro: Route 47 runs 61.09 miles between Pamplin City and South Hill, with its entire length designated a Virginia Byway. Near Pamplin, it parallels a railway and follows the boundary between Charlotte and Prince Edward counties. Farther south, the highway follows the drainage divide between the Meherrin River to the north and the Roanoke to the south.

At the northern end, Pamplin was a stop on the Southside Railroad in the mid-19th century. The rail corridor from Burkeville to Pamplin later became High Bridge Trail State Park, and an extension into town opened in April 2024.

For a southbound drive, leave US 460 Business at Pamplin and follow Route 47 toward Cullen and Charlotte Court House. Beyond the county seat, cross Roanoke Creek and continue through Drakes Branch to Craftons Gate. Chase City brings the route onto Main Street and Second Street, then the road follows the divide through Wightman to South Hill’s Atlantic Street.

moments.title: Pamplin City
moments.text: A former railway corridor now brings walkers toward Pamplin’s Main Street business district. The town was a Southside Railroad stop in the mid-19th century, and the rail line from Burkeville to Pamplin became High Bridge Trail State Park. Pamplin’s railway history also includes the Atlantic, Mississippi and Ohio Railroad, which succeeded the Southside in 1870, before later Norfolk and Western ownership. The extension into town opened on April 22, 2024. Beside Business 460 is another part of Pamplin’s industrial past: the Pamplin Pipe Factory, formerly the largest clay pipe factory in the United States. It entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

moments.title: Charlotte Court House
moments.text: The courthouse’s white columns belong to a building erected in 1821–1823, using plans supplied by Thomas Jefferson. Its brick, temple-form design became a model for Virginia court buildings in the 1830s and 1840s. Patrick Henry’s last political speech came earlier, in March 1799, at Charlotte Courthouse, when he opposed the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions. The present building therefore postdates that speech. The complex also includes a brick law office and a late-Victorian clerk’s office with an entrance tower and arch. The courthouse stands at the center of a historic district that also includes churches, a former county jail and the county library.

moments.title: Chase City
moments.text: Chase City’s former high school has become housing, while its brick Colonial Revival buildings remain part of the town’s architecture. The school building was erected in 1908 and expanded in 1917. It closed in 1980; in 1991 the complex was rehabilitated as apartments for elderly residents. The former school is now known as Maple Manor Apartments, and the complex entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1997. A separate brick building constructed for vocational agriculture classes in 1917 also belongs to the complex. The town itself was incorporated in 1873 and named for Salmon P. Chase, Lincoln’s treasury secretary and a United States chief justice.
